My doctor wants me to cut back on salt, so my wife and I are overhauling how we cook. I take lisinopril and spironolactone for heart failure, and my last blood test put my potassium at the very top of normal.

So far the change has been harder than I expected. We're a family that loves savoury food: crisps on the sofa, soy sauce on everything, and a particular brand of stock cubes my wife swears by. Last weekend we tried making a roast chicken with nothing but herbs, and she announced it tasted like cardboard, although she ate all of it. The supermarket near us has a whole aisle of seasonings I've never explored, with blends from every region and a wall of pepper grinders. I'm also trying to walk more, so I've been going out for half an hour after dinner, and last Wednesday I took the long way around the park and met a neighbour whose dog is the size of a small pony. In a few weeks we're hosting my in-laws for dinner, and I'd like the cooking to be good enough that nobody notices anything has changed. My wife has been keeping a list on the fridge of recipes we'd like to try, and the pot roast is at the top.

What should I stock up on at the supermarket tomorrow to replace the salt at the table and in cooking?

A) Herb blends, garlic, lemon zest and pepper
B) Let me talk it over with you a bit more first
C) A potassium-based salt substitute

I'm planning a road trip from Denver to Portland and back in September, roughly 4,000 miles round trip, and I'm trying to keep the cost down. The car is my leased Mazda. My lease allows 12,000 miles a year at 40 cents a mile beyond that, and the odometer shows I've already used 11,100 with five months left.

The trip itself has been on my list for years. A college friend moved to Portland two summers ago and keeps sending me pictures of waterfalls and food trucks, and I finally got three weeks of vacation approved. I'd like to stop in Salt Lake City on the way out to see the salt flats, and then spend a few days in Boise, where another friend has a spare room and a very opinionated beagle. I've been listening to podcasts and building a playlist for the drive, and I bought a new set of wiper blades and a tire pressure gauge as a gesture of responsibility. My sister thinks I'm crazy to drive that far alone, but I like the idea of stopping whenever something looks interesting. I'm not sure whether I'll camp or stay in motels, and I haven't decided what snacks are acceptable for a road trip, other than that gummy bears are mandatory. I've also been told the weather in the mountains can change quickly in September, so I'm packing both a rain jacket and a hat.

Which is the cheapest way to do this trip?

A) Rent a car for the ten days for about $780
B) Drive my leased Mazda, with fuel and motels coming to about $650
C) Let me dig out my lease paperwork first
